channel.title: Brazil Elections 2026
channel.description: Real-time monitoring of the 2026 Brazilian presidential elections.

item.title: Lula terá dificuldades para governar com Congresso fortalecido pela direita
item.description: Lula will face governing difficulties with Congress strengthened by the right and the PL. Despite Flávio Bolsonaro's defeat, the party elected 121 federal deputies and will have 28 senators from 2027, the largest benches in both Houses.

item.title: Com mais de 60 milhões de votos, Lula tem maior votação da história do país
item.description: Lula (PT) won the presidential runoff with over 60 million votes, becoming the candidate with the highest vote count in Brazilian history. With 99% of polling stations counted, he defeated Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), who came in second place. This result marks a historic victory in the Brazilian electoral landscape.

item.title: Lula indicará ao menos mais 4 ministros ao Supremo até 2030
item.description: Lula is expected to appoint at least 4 more ministers to the Supreme Court by 2030, totaling at least 13 nominations. In addition to the vacancy opened by Barroso's retirement, the PT president will have to choose successors for three more ministers who will retire during his term.

item.title: De pacote eleitoral a exército digital: Como Lula conseguiu virada inédita
item.description: Lula secured re-election by combining digital campaigning led by André Janones, street mobilization, and targeted voter incentives.

item.title: Janones descontruiu comunicação de Lula e assumiu protagonismo na campanha
item.description: André Janones hosted a 24-hour live stream following the debate between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, gaining prominence in the campaign and taking a leading role in political communication.

item.title: Flávio perde para Lula e bolsonarismo é derrotado ao tentar voltar ao poder
item.description: Lula defeats Flávio Bolsonaro in a historic victory that prevents the return of Bolsonarism to power.

item.title: Lula é reeleito, supera votação de 2022 e ultrapassa 63 milhões de votos
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) was reelected as Brazil's president with 64,156,472 votes, surpassing his 2022 performance. He secured 51.76% of valid votes against 48.24% for Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), securing his fourth term and becoming the first president democratically elected four times.

item.title: Nunca antes na história deste país: Lula vira no 2º turno e é reeleito
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) was re-elected to the presidency in a historic new term, becoming the first candidate to overturn a first-round deficit and win in the second round. He secured 51.42% of valid votes, driven by strong mobilization from the PT, particularly among voters who abstained in the first round. Senator Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) lost the race despite leading in the first round with 47.03% of the votes.

item.title: Lula amplia votação e mantém vitória sobre Flávio na capital paulista
item.description: Lula defeated Flávio Bolsonaro in São Paulo's capital in the runoff with 55.48% of the vote versus 44.52%, reinforcing his standing in Brazil's largest city. The win was marked by large pro-Lula rallies on Avenida Paulista.

item.title: De metalúrgico a presidente pela 4ª vez, relembre a trajetória de Lula
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) was reelected president for the fourth time, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in a historic turnaround in the second round. At 81 years old, Lula is the oldest president in Brazilian history and will allow for a long-term government partnership until 2031.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro é o 1º a liderar no 1º turno e perder corrida ao Planalto
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) became the first presidential candidate to lead in the first round and lose the election since the return to democracy, defeated by Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT). Lula's victory broke a 35-year streak in which all first-round leaders had won the second round, including historic elections from 1989 to 2022.

item.title: Com vitória de Lula, Brasil freia onda pró-Trump na América Latina
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva's victory over Flávio Bolsonaro in the 2026 presidential election represents a brake on the right-wing wave and Donald Trump's project in Latin America. The result reflects a strategic shift on the continent, with strengthening of progressive governments. This outcome is likely to influence regional foreign policy and Brazil's international relations.

item.title: Veja os horários das viradas na apuração presidencial entre Lula e Flávio
item.description: The runoff vote count showed lead changes between Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro, according to TSE data. The shifts occurred throughout the count, reflecting the competitiveness of the race.

item.title: Lula, la épica de la izquierda mundial
item.description: The article highlights the epic trajectory of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva, emphasizing the influence of his mother, Doña Lindu, in his campaigns and speeches. It reinforces the image of Lula as a leader who combines sovereignty, democracy and multilateralism with a personal narrative of social overcoming.

item.title: Saiba quem ganha e quem perde com a vitória de Lula
item.description: Lula's reelection benefits vulnerable groups and maintains current environmental policies, while penalizing high-income sectors with higher taxes. The congressional center and figures like Davi Alcolumbre, Hugo Motta and André Janones gain influence in Congress, while the STF and Senate avoid impeachment risks. The economy faces high interest rates and worsening public accounts.

item.title: Lula terá Trump como principal desafio externo e apostará em diálogo após embates na eleição
item.description: Lula will begin his fourth term dealing with the challenge of managing relations with Donald Trump, with whom he had clashes during the election campaign, betting on dialogue as the main strategy in foreign policy.

item.title: Clã Bolsonaro perde 2ª eleição presidencial seguida para Lula
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva won his second consecutive presidential election against a Bolsonaro family candidate, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro, chosen by jailed Jair Bolsonaro on charges of attempted coup. The result confirms Lula's fourth term and ends the Bolsonaro family's attempt to return to power after the 2018 loss.

item.title: Fim da eleição define composição do Senado em 2027, com 13 partidos
item.description: With the conclusion of the 2026 elections, the composition of the Senate from 2027 is virtually set, led by the PL with 29 seats. The scenario reflects October election results, 2023 terms through 2031, and replacements due to gubernatorial elections. The renewal is significant, with 74% of contested terms filled by new senators. The composition still depends on the TSE decision regarding Deltan Dallagnol's candidacy.

item.title: Apoiadores de Lula comemoram virada na apuração na av. Paulista, em São Paulo
item.description: Supporters of Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva celebrated his re-election on Paulista Avenue in São Paulo after the vote turnaround in the 2026 runoff count.

item.title: Lula supera erros, mas encara última dança difícil
item.description: Lula defeats Flávio Bolsonaro in the second round, opening a new chapter in Brazilian democracy. The PT victory ends Flávio's political career, who struggled to build his own narrative. The 2026 electoral scenario shows persistent polarization and the importance of experienced leaders for governance.

item.title: Cadu de Lula é eleito governador do Rio Grande do Norte
item.description: Cadu de Lula (PT) was elected governor of Rio Grande do Norte with 50.71% of valid votes against Allyson Bezerra (União Brasil), who received 49.29%. The victory keeps the PT in power in the state after two terms of Fátima Bezerra, who left in 2026 to run for governor. Cadu, former Finance Secretary, had the support of President Lula and the Time que Cuida coalition.

item.title: Ou a gente ganha, ou a gente ganha, diz Nikolas Ferreira
item.description: Deputy Nikolas Ferreira (PL-MG) criticized the STF's decision to extend the 2026 election vote until 7 PM, requested by Lula's campaign (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro's team (PL). He referred to Minister Cristiano Zanin as 'another impeachment' and shared comparisons with Venezuelan elections. The extension was granted following claims of voting access difficulties in multiple regions.

item.title: Flávio Bolsonaro repete feito de Jair e vence Lula no estado de São Paulo
item.description: Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) defeated Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) in São Paulo in both rounds of the presidential election, mirroring his father Jair Bolsonaro's victory. With 98.47% of polling stations counted, Flávio secured 53.94% of the votes against Lula's 45.95%. São Paulo, home to 34 million voters, is the country's largest electoral college.

item.title: Reeleito para quarto mandato, Lula terá Congresso com maioria da oposição e precisará negociar para aprovar projetos
item.description: Lula was reelected for his fourth presidential term, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro, but will face a Congress dominated by the opposition, complicating the approval of his agenda. With the growth of the PL and centrist parties' backing of the defeated candidate, the new government will need broad negotiations to pass priorities such as free public transport and labor reform. Despite challenges, Lula has approached legislative leaders and approved significant reforms.

item.title: Reeleito, Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva governará o Brasil pela quarta vez
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) was re-elected president of Brazil in 2026, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro (PL-RJ) in the runoff. He became the first politician to win four presidential terms and defied polls favoring his opponent. However, Lula faces challenges like opposition majority in Congress and security crisis.

item.title: Lula é reeleito presidente do Brasil em virada histórica
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva was reelected president of Brazil with 51.75% of valid votes in the runoff, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro. His victory was marked by strong social media mobilization, led by André Janones with the 'Lula Army', and street protests in several cities. Key proposals include raising the minimum wage, investing in national defense, creating a Ministry of Public Security, expanding cancer care, and broadening the 'Pé-de-Meia' program to higher education.

item.title: Cadu de Lula vence no 2º turno e é eleito governador do RN
item.description: Cadu de Lula (PT) won against Allyson Bezerra (União Brasil) in the second round and was elected governor of Rio Grande do Norte. Despite trailing slightly in the first round (36.61% vs 36.69%), Cadu advanced to the final and turned the race around. An economist and former Finance Secretary, Cadu leads a political project aligned with the PT and President Lula.

item.title: Em virada inédita, Lula vence Flávio Bolsonaro em votação marcada por caos eleitoral
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) was reelected president with 51.75% of valid votes, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), in an election marked by electoral chaos and voting hour extension. The victory represents a historic turnaround, the first time a front-runner in the first round lost in the second.

item.title: Quantos anos Lula terá quando terminar o quarto mandato em 2031?
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva will be 85 years old upon completing his fourth presidential term in 2031. Born on October 27, 1945, he will take office on January 5, 2027, at age 81, following his reelection in 2026.

item.title: Articulador de Lula com empresários e negociador no tarifaço, Alckmin é reeleito vice-presidente
item.description: Geraldo Alckmin (PSB) was re-elected vice president on Lula's ticket, solidifying an unprecedented alliance with the PT after decades of political rivalry. Former São Paulo governor and ex-presidential candidate from PSDB, Alckmin will begin his second term as vice president, marking a major shift in his political career.

item.title: Lula é reeleito aos 80 anos e se torna novamente o presidente mais velho da história do Brasil; veja ranking
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) was reelected president of Brazil at the age of 80, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the 2026 runoff, becoming the oldest person to win a presidential election in the country's history. With this win, Lula breaks his own record, beginning his fourth term on January 5, 2027, at 81 years old.

item.title: Lula é eleito pela 4ª vez e supera recorde de longevidade na democracia
item.description: Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) was elected president of Brazil for the fourth time, becoming the first politician chosen four times by direct vote. With 51.76% of the votes, he defeated Flávio Bolsonaro (PL), who secured 48.24%. Upon completing his fourth term, Lula will have served 16 years as president, surpassing the longevity record in Brazilian democracy.

item.title: Lula poderá disputar a Presidência novamente em 2030? Entenda
item.description: Following Lula's reelection in 2026, he will not be eligible to run for President in 2030 due to the constitutional rule allowing only one consecutive reelection. However, Lula could run again in future elections after the 2031 term ends.

item.title: Quantas eleições Lula disputou e quantas venceu? Relembre
item.description: Lula ran in nine elections throughout his career—eight for the presidency and one for São Paulo governor—winning five, including a hypothetical 2026 victory. He was elected president four times: in 2002, 2006, 2022, and 2026, as outlined in the article.

item.title: TSE avisou seções sobre prorrogação às 17h49
item.description: The TSE informed electoral sections at 5:49 PM about the extension of voting until 7 PM, following a decision by Minister Cristiano Zanin at the request of the campaigns of Lula and Flávio Bolsonaro. Part of the sections had already closed; only the open ones remained active. The extension was due to issues such as lack of transportation, rains, and power outages.

item.title: Com Lula reeleito, Janja segue como primeira-dama do Brasil; conheça a trajetória da socióloga
item.description: With Lula's re-election in 2026, Janja remains as First Lady, standing out for her political trajectory from age 17 as a PT member. Known nationally after her relationship with Lula in 2019, she participated in official agendas and international trips, generating criticism about the limits of her role.

item.title: Lula conquista virada inédita no segundo turno e é reeleito para 4º mandato
item.description: Lula was reelected for a fourth term after a historic comeback in the runoff, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro with 51.79% of the vote. With over 64.2 million votes, Lula achieved the highest electoral result for a president in Brazil's history. The PT campaign reorganized after trailing in the first round, adopting new digital communication strategies.

item.title: Lula vira eleição e conquista quarto mandato à Presidência
item.description: Lula (PT) was reelected for a fourth presidential term, defeating Flávio Bolsonaro (PL) in the 2026 runoff. With 98.76% of polling stations counted, Lula secured 51.75% of valid votes against 48.25% for his opponent. This victory marks a return to PT leadership following the previous administration.

item.title: Decisão do STF causa confusão em locais de votação: 'Não tem como reabrir'
item.description: The STF decision to extend voting hours caused confusion in São Paulo, Rio de Janeiro, and Belo Horizonte, with voters unable to cast ballots after 6 PM and poll workers lacking clear guidance. Minister Cristiano Zanin was mentioned as responsible for the ruling.

item.title: Para que o TSE se um ministro do STF pode mudar as regras do jogo? Questiona Sóstenes
item.description: Sóstenes Cavalcante, the PL leader in the Chamber of Deputies, questioned the Supreme Court's role after Justice Cristiano Zanin ordered the extension of voting hours until 7 PM nationwide, accusing the STF of undue interference in the electoral process.

item.title: Em Salvador, seções chegaram a reabrir portões após decisão de Zanin
item.description: In Salvador, some polling stations reopened after Minister Cristiano Zanin, of the Brazilian Supreme Court, extended voting hours until 7 PM nationwide. Meanwhile, other locations had already closed, making it impossible to accept new votes in those areas.

item.title: Resultados de las elecciones en Brasil, en vivo|Cierran las urnas en Brasil y empieza el conteo de votos
item.description: Polling stations closed across Brazil on Sunday, marking the start of vote counting in the most competitive presidential runoff in the nation's history. The race pits President Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva against far-right senator Flávio Bolsonaro, with polls indicating a technical tie following Bolsonaro's unexpected victory in the first round.

item.title: Decisão de Zanin exige explicações claras, diz Tarcísio
item.description: The governor of São Paulo, Tarcísio de Freitas, criticized Supreme Court Minister Cristiano Zanin's decision to extend the vote, demanding clarifications on its basis and execution. He emphasized the need for respect, transparency, and legal certainty in Brazil.

item.title: Marçal critica prorrogação da votação e questiona decisão do STF
item.description: Pablo Marçal criticized the extension of voting hours for the second round of elections and questioned the Supreme Federal Court's decision, arguing that the measure would not be necessary nationwide.

item.title: Após prorrogação, Lula e aliados pedem que eleitores votem
item.description: President Lula and allies urged voters to cast ballots after Supreme Court extended voting hours to 7 PM nationwide due to public transportation shortages affecting at least nine states.

item.title: Eleições: PGR foi contra estender horário de votação para 19h na Bahia
item.description: The Deputy Attorney General for Electoral Matters, Alexandre Espinosa Bravo Barbosa, opposed extending voting hours to 7 PM in Bahia, advocating for maintaining the legal 5 PM deadline and investigating the facts. Despite this, Supreme Federal Court Minister Cristiano Zanin decided to extend voting hours until 7 PM nationwide. Zanin's decision particularly affected cases involving transportation and logistical failures, such as in Salvador, which led to the arrest of Municipal Mobility Secretary Pablo Souza.

item.title: Tarcísio nega problemas de transporte em SP e critica decisão de Zanin de estender votação
item.description: São Paulo Governor Tarcísio de Freitas denied public transportation issues and criticized Minister Cristiano Zanin's decision to extend voting hours until 7 PM, accusing the judiciary of institutionalizing the crisis. He claimed the narrative of transportation failures is an attempt to create controversy before the elections.

item.title: Eleitores da BA e SP ficam sem votar por urnas fechadas, apesar de horário
item.description: Voters in Salvador and São Paulo were prevented from casting ballots despite a last-minute extension of voting hours to 7 PM ordered by Supreme Court justice Cristiano Zanin. Videos show sealed polling stations and lack of public transport. The ruling applies only to sites where voting had not yet finished.

item.title: AO VIVO resultado das eleições 2026 – acompanhe a apuração da disputa entre Flávio Bolsonaro e Lula no 2º turno
item.description: Over 158.7 million eligible voters in Brazil head to the polls for the 2026 second-round elections, featuring a presidential race between Luiz Inácio Lula da Silva (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Gubernatorial races in six states are also on the ballot. Voting takes place from 8am to 5pm, with live coverage starting at 4pm on YouTube and the JOTA website.

item.title: Mesários "perdidos" esperam orientação sobre reabertura de urnas em SP
item.description: Following the STF decision to extend voting hours from 5 PM to 7 PM, several polling stations in São Paulo kept their doors closed due to lack of guidance from the Regional Electoral Court (TRE). Poll workers reported confusion and uncertainty, closing the ballot boxes without knowing whether they should reopen, as the TRE had not specifically informed the affected zones. The decision was prompted by complaints of reduced bus fleets, but communication delays caused frustration among voters and poll workers.
